observations: Photo 0 shows a dark-screened LG-branded LCD monitor (logo visible on bottom bezel) resting on a stack of metal pots/trays, not a proper desk stand.
Top-left of the monitor bezel shows partial text, possibly 'FLATRON' style branding, but the exact model number is not legible.
A black full-size keyboard sits in front, no brand or model markings are readable in the photo.
Monitor screen is off/blank, so no indication of power-on, picture quality, or dead pixels.
No power cable, video cable (VGA/HDMI), or stand/base is clearly visible; the monitor appears propped on cookware rather than its own stand.
General surface dust and a worn, slightly discoloured keyboard suggest heavy prior use.
Background shows a room with plastic chair and rug, consistent with a home resale, not a shop.

identity.kind: LCD monitor and keyboard (scrap/for-parts computer peripherals)

claims.claim: Scrap LG monitor and keyboard available for sale
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows the items but the screen is off and no power test or cable is shown, so functional state (scrap vs working) cannot be confirmed from the image alone.
Photo 0 bottom bezel clearly shows 'LG' logo.

risks.risk: Monitor may not power on or display an image (seller already labels it 'scrap').
risks.proof: A photo or short clip of the monitor powered on showing a picture on screen.

risks.risk: Missing power adapter and video cable (VGA/HDMI) needed to use the monitor.
risks.proof: A photo showing the power brick and video cable included in the sale.
risks.if_unproven: priced as monitor only, no accessories

risks.risk: Keyboard condition and connector type (PS/2 vs USB) unknown; some keys may be worn or non-responsive.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the keyboard connector and a clip of keys being pressed with visible response (e.g., on screen or LED).

risks.risk: Physical damage (cracked screen, bent stand, broken hinge) could be hidden by the dark screen and awkward propping.
risks.proof: A well-lit photo from multiple angles showing the screen surface and the monitor's own stand/base.

proof_requests: Video or photo of the monitor powered on with a visible picture.
Photo of the monitor's own stand/base (not propped on pots) and the rear ports.
Photo of power adapter and video cable included in the sale.
Close-up photo of the keyboard connector type and a short clip showing key responsiveness.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as an LG monitor and a generic keyboard, both explicitly described by the seller as scrap; absent any proof of power-on function or included cables, the fair approach is to price them at worst case as non-working, parts-only peripherals.
